articles.title: India has around 440 space technology startups - ANI News
articles.content: New Delhi [India], August 16 (ANI): Around 440 space technology startups are registered in India, as per the DPIIT Start-up India Portal. IN-SPACe has granted 113 authorisations to 52 Non-Government Entities (NGEs) to carry out various space activities, out of which 18 are start-ups, Minister of State for Atomic Energy and Space Dr Jitendra Singh told the Rajya Sabha in a written reply earlier this week. The 18 start-ups are Agnikul Cosmos Pvt Ltd, Akshath Aerospace Private Limited, Azista BST, Bellatrix Aerospace Pvt Ltd, Cosmoserv Space India Private Limited, Dhruva Space Private Limited, Digantara Research and Technologies Pvt. Ltd, GalaxEye Space Solutions Private Limited, HEX20Labs India Pvt ltd, Inorbit Space Telecommunications Private Limited, Manastu Space Technologies Private Limited, NSpace Tech India Private Limited, OrbitAID Aerospace Private Limited, PierSight Space Private Limited, PixxelSpace India Private Limited, Skyroot Aerospace Private Limited, Space Kidz India and TakeMe2Space Technologies Pvt. Ltd. The applications for usage and access to ISRO infrastructure (including the launch pads at ISRO's Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota ) are processed as per the standard SOP based on the application received by IN-SPACe on its Digital Platform and the readiness aspects are reviewed by an Expert Committee of IN-SPACe , the minister said. Two commercial rockets are proposed to be launched by Indian private companies in FY 26-27. For FY 27-28, the Launch manifest is yet to be approved by IN-SPACe . The minister said over six launches may be undertaken by Indian private companies. According to government data, private investment in India's space sector surged nearly six-fold, climbing from USD 100.5 million in 2021-22 to USD 618.5 million by March 31, 2026, with USD 187 million recorded during 2026 alone. The Union Cabinet led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi took a decision in June 2020 to open up the Space sector and enable the participation of Indian private sector in the entire gamut of space activities. To facilitate private sector participation, the government created the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre ( IN-SPACe ), as a single-window, independent, nodal agency which functions as an autonomous agency in Department of Space (DOS). By mid-2026, 113 authorisations had been granted to 52 Non-Government Entities (NGEs) out of which 18 are start-ups for satellite operations, payload establishment and launch services. (ANI)

articles.title: India Space Journey: Moon, Mars & Gaganyaan Missions | ISRO Capability
articles.content: English News Tech science India Space Journey: Moon, Mars & Gaganyaan Missions | ISRO Capability From Aryabhata to Gaganyaan, nation's independent capability: How India’s space journey is reaching for the Moon, Mars and beyond 1 day ago Author: Samira Siddiqui Copy link When India looks back at 80 years of independence, one of its most remarkable journeys has taken place far above Earth. From a country that once relied heavily on foreign launchers to put satellites into orbit, India has built the capability to launch its own spacecraft, explore the Moon and Mars, study the Sun, perform complex operations in orbit and prepare to send humans into space. India’s space story is therefore no longer just about launching satellites. It is about building the capability to explore, operate and eventually live beyond Earth. From Aryabhata to a homegrown launch capability Aryabhata, India's first satellite, was launched on April 19, 1975, from the Volgograd Launch Station (Kapustin Yar) in the Soviet Union using a Kosmos-3M launch vehicle. India’s space programme took an important early step with Aryabhata, the country’s first satellite, launched in 1975. It marked the beginning of India’s journey towards developing its own expertise in spacecraft and space science. The next decades saw India build increasingly capable launch vehicles and satellites. The Satellite Launch Vehicle (SLV-3) demonstrated India’s ability to place a satellite in orbit using an indigenous rocket, while the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) eventually became one of ISRO’s most dependable launchers. This foundation allowed India to move from learning how to reach space to using space for communication, weather forecasting, Earth observation, navigation, and scientific research. Chandrayaan put India on the Moon India’s lunar exploration began with Chandrayaan-1 in 2008. The mission transformed India from a country developing space technology into an active participant in planetary science. Among its significant findings was evidence of water molecules and hydroxyl on the lunar surface. Chandrayaan-2, launched in 2019, went further with an orbiter, lander, and rover. Although the lander could not achieve a soft landing, its orbiter continued its scientific work around the Moon. Then came Chandrayaan-3 in 2023. Its successful landing of the Vikram lander and deployment of the Pragyan rover near the lunar south polar region marked a historic achievement. India became the fourth country to demonstrate a soft landing on the Moon and the first to land in the southern polar region. The mission also demonstrated technologies needed for future planetary exploration. The next step is even more ambitious. Chandrayaan-4 is designed to collect lunar samples and bring them back to Earth. That means India will have to master a far more complex chain of operations, from landing and collecting samples on the Moon to returning the material safely to Earth. From Mars to the Sun The Mars Orbiter Mission, or Mangalyaan, entered Martian orbit in 2014, making India the first Asian nation to reach Mars orbit on its first attempt. The spacecraft was designed for a six-month mission but remained operational for years, demonstrating...

articles.title: Filling vacant posts government's priority: CM Shivakumar - The New Indian Express
articles.content: BENGALURU: Chief Minister DK Shivakumar announced on Saturday that he will soon launch the ‘Chief Minister’s Jobs Mission’, under which vacant posts in government departments will be filled on priority. He stated this during his maiden Independence Day speech as chief minister at Manekshaw Parade Grounds in Bengaluru. He said the government has already begun the process of filling 72,000 key vacancies, and in the next six months, a notification will be issued to fill the posts. Targeting the youth and students, Shivakumar said that a new initiative, ‘Yuva Udyoga Setu’, will be launched and a comprehensive digital platform developed to connect youngsters with employment opportunities in the private sector. He also announced ‘Udyoga Nidhi’ to provide incentives to entrepreneurs for creating new employment opportunities. Govt plans AI training from Class 6 at schools The ‘Udyoga Nidhi’ scheme is aimed at the 10 most backward districts of the state and will offer Rs 2,500 incentive per month for every new job created for up to two years. “This will create one lakh new jobs,” the CM said. Under a new initiative, ‘Vidyarthi Sahaya Hastha ‘, students studying in rural government schools from Class 1 to 10 will be provided 7.5% reservation along with the existing 15%. “This will give them access to quality professional higher education like medical and engineering courses,” he said. He mentioned AI Akshara Abhiyana and Coding Gurukula programmes to introduce artificial intelligence education in schools across the state and equip students to compete globally. “AI education will be introduced in all schools from Class 6. The government is also working to establish India’s first government-owned AI university in Bengaluru,” he said. To improve the quality of schools and colleges, an expert committee has been constituted to reform the examination system and submit a report in two months. He said that through his vision of “Yuva Karnataka, Nava Bharat”, a target has been set to take the state’s economy to $3 trillion by 2047. He said 10,000 Bharat Jodo Yuva Sanghas (clubs) will be set up across Karnataka and each club will receive an annual grant of Rs 10 lakh, for which the government will allocate Rs 1,000 crore. Addressing concerns of a large section of motorists and their struggle to get insurance claims during difficult times, he said the state government will set up the Karnataka State Motor Vehicle Insurance Corporation. To de-stress and decongest Bengaluru, five Global Technology Centres will be set up in Kalaburagi, Belagavi, Hubballi-Dharwad, Mangaluru and Mysuru under the Beyond Bengaluru initiative, he declared. Reaching out to farmers, he announced the ‘Mukhyamantri Raitha Chaitanya’ scheme, which will give out real-time data on crops, pests and disease outbreaks. Under the ‘Raitha Mitra’ initiative, small farmers will receive machinery on rent and farmers with three acres or less will get a 50% subsidy on rentals. Focusing on Bengaluru, he announced tree parks on the lines of Lalbagh at Turahalli mini forest, Thottikallu Falls, Nettigere, BM Kaval forest area, Basavanthara and Mandur-Jyothipura on Bengaluru outskirts....

articles.title: Karnataka eyes USD 3 trillion economy by 2047, Shivakumar unveils jobs and AI plan
articles.content: Our Special Correspondent Published 16.08.26, 04:28 AM Karnataka chief minister D.K. Shivakumar on Saturday announced welfare and industry initiatives, from filling 72,000 government vacancies to establishing India’s first public AI University, and said his goal was to propel the state towards a $3-trillion economy by 2047. His announcements coincided with the Independence Day celebrations at the Field Marshal Manekshaw Parade Ground in Bengaluru. The event began with the recital of the national song, Vande Mataram , in full. ADVERTISEMENT During Shivakumar’s swearing-in on June 3, too, Vande Mataram had been sung in full. In his first Independence Day speech as chief minister, Shivakumar said the development of Karnataka and that of India complemented each other. “The government’s goal is to further develop the strength of Karnataka, which is showing the way to the country in knowledge, science, technology, industry, agriculture, economy and culture,” he said. “Karnataka’s per capita income has reached ₹ 4.33 lakh, and the state is ranked second in GST and income tax collections. The target is to take Karnataka’s economy to $3 trillion… by 2047 by investing in education, health, agriculture, industry and infrastructure.” Shivakumar announced a Chief Minister Employment Commitment to generate jobs and fill 72,000 vacant government posts. He promised to create 1 lakh jobs within the next two years. He also announced an AI Akshara Abhiyaan and a Coding Gurukul to facilitate skill development among children and the youth. “Our motto is ‘Young Karnataka, New India’. More funds are being provided to shape the future of the youth,” the chief minister said. “AI is being introduced in the state’s schools from Class VI onwards, along with the AI Akshara Abhiyan and Coding Gurukul. Bengaluru is going to have the first AI university, which will also have AI hubs.” In apparent acknowledgement of the widespread complaints about Bengaluru losing its green lung, Shivakumar announced five large tree parks and the rejuvenation of seven lakes in the city. He said the Hesaraghatta Lake, Bettada Kote Lake, Hoskote Lake, Ele Mallappa Shetty Lake, Bannerghatta Lake, Bagalur Lake and Byramangala Lake would be developed for groundwater recharge, which would reduce the drinking water scarcity in Bangalore.

articles.title: Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar announces AI education from Class 6, India's first public AI ...
articles.content: Bengaluru ( Karnataka ) [India], August 15 (ANI): Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar on Saturday announced a major push to make the state's students future-ready with new AI and digital education initiatives. Calling it "Your era: A new era," the Chief Minister said the government is designing a wide range of programs to prepare today's youth to compete successfully on the global stage and shape a new future for themselves. AI education will be introduced from Class VI onwards in all schools across the state. Two major initiatives, including AI Akshara Abhiyana and Coding Gurukul, were announced. Free 'Coding Gurukul' special classes will provide every student an opportunity to learn AI and coding skills. The state's first public AI University will be established in Bengaluru . AI Certificate Courses will commence by January 2027. AI Hubs will be set up across Karnataka to expand access to AI training and innovation. The Chief Minister stressed that improving the quality of school education is of utmost importance. Over the next two years, 1,000 government schools will be developed into Karnataka Public Schools with modern infrastructure, bilingual education, digital classrooms, vocational education and student transportation under one roof from LKG to Class XII. The initiative will benefit nearly 10 lakh students, he said. He also noted that free bus travel has been extended to school and college students across the state, with more than 6 lakh free bus passes already issued. The government said the initiatives are aimed at equipping Karnataka 's youth with 21st-century skills and bridging the digital divide. Earlier, Shivakumar attended the Independence Day celebrations held at the Congress office in Bengaluru . KPCC President BK Hariprasad hoisted the national flag there on the occassion. Along with the Chief Minister, former Chief Minister Veerappa Moily, party leaders, and Congress workers participated in the programme. (ANI)

articles.title: Redcliffe Labs and Skyroot Aerospace launch India's first diagnostics & space sciences collaboration
articles.content: August 14, 2026 | Friday | News In a landmark initiative coming together of India’s healthcare and private space ecosystems, Redcliffe Labs, one of India’s fastest-growing omnichannel diagnostic service providers, and Skyroot Aerospace, India’s first private company to reach orbit, have joined hands to explore the future of diagnostics in space. The collaboration brings together two distinctly Indian capabilities diagnostic science and space technology to study how diagnostic reagents perform under the extreme conditions of Low Earth Orbit, while exploring how the learnings could advance diagnostics on Earth. The first step is DRIFT-1, which will place Redcliffe Labs' dry diagnostic reagents in Low Earth Orbit for 90 days, alongside an identical ground control. Comparing the two will help establish how the space environment affects reagent stability and performance and generate a flight-heritage dataset for the technology. The initiative extends beyond the first mission, with potential applications spanning space-enabled diagnostics, astronaut health, life sciences and microgravity research, including future point-of-care diagnostic solutions for human spaceflight such as Gaganyaan and the Bharatiya Antariksh Station. For Redcliffe Labs, the opportunity lies in turning this data into knowledge that can inform more resilient diagnostic technologies for challenging environments on Earth, including settings where conventional infrastructure or cold-chain availability is limited.

articles.title: 'The Bose Network', India's first hybrid ai drama - Adgully.com
articles.content: Joy Sengupta leads the cast as Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, with an accomplished ensemble and award-winning creative talent bringing the sweeping historical thriller to life. Story TV, India’s leading microdrama platform from Eloelo Group, will premiere The Bose Network at midnight on August 15. Structured as a continuous chase rather than a conventional biopic, the historical thriller dramatises one of the most daring escapes in Indian history. Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose’s 1941 disappearance from British house arrest in Calcutta and the 9,000-kilometre journey across four countries, adopting four identities to raise India’s own army against the British Empire. The Bose Network is also India’s first microdrama series with an AI-integrated production pipeline. 1940s Calcutta, the Frontier Kabul, wartime Berlin, the interiors of two submarines and scores of other historical references were reconstructed in post-production using Eloelo’s AI expertise, bringing a period drama to the vertical screen at a scale the format has not previously attempted. Joy Sengupta , while reflecting on his portrayal of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, said, “Every Indian carries an image of Bose with them, the uniform, the spectacles, the voice on the radio. But growing up as a Bengali, especially with a father who was a die-hard Bose admirer, I grew up surrounded by Bose, his convictions, his actions, and the folklore around him. As an adult and as an actor, I also learnt to look beyond the folklore and understand the circumstances that shaped him and the context in which his choices were made. Playing Bose, for me, was about finding the human within the story and bringing out the human side of the man behind the epic. Because that to me is the job of a true actor. I hope what remains on screen is not just an impersonation of an icon, but a man with his loneliness, his stubbornness, and his unwavering belief that India would be free in his lifetime.” The series spans the period from Bose's escape from surveillance at his family home in January 1941 to the events of August 1945. From the escape through Gomoh, Peshawar and Kabul to his years in Berlin, from secret radio broadcasts and a submarine crossing to a government in exile and the final years in Asia. The Bose Network traces not just one man's journey but the network he built to create it: the couriers, safe houses, sympathetic legations, radio operators, prisoners of war turned soldiers, and volunteers across four countries, who each moved him one stage further. It moves through some of the most remarkable and least-explored chapters of his life. The Bose Network is written and directed by Lalit Marathe, one of the writers of Swades(2004), widely regarded as one of Hindi cinema's most enduring patriotic dramas. “A period film is not built on research alone; it is also built on imagination. You are trying to recreate a Calcutta that no living person remembers. The glow of a streetlamp at two in the morning, the silence inside a house where everyone...

articles.title: India's first Vande Bharat freight train clocks 130 kmph in trial - News Arena
articles.content: India’s first Vande Bharat freight train has undergone a 130 kmph trial run on the Kota-Rohal Khurd section of West Central Railway, marking a step towards faster movement of parcels and other goods by rail. The trial was conducted as part of technical testing, with teams from the Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO) and Integral Coach Factory (ICF) present to assess the train’s performance at high speed. Railway officials tested several electrical, propulsion and safety systems during the run, including regenerative energy, thermal capacity, traction, braking and jerk levels under loaded conditions. The regenerative energy test assessed how efficiently the train can recover electrical energy while braking. The thermal capacity test examined the performance of the electrical and propulsion systems during high-speed operation. Traction and braking tests were carried out to assess the train’s pulling and stopping capabilities, while jerk tests examined the smoothness of acceleration and deceleration when the train is carrying a load. Based on the Vande Bharat series, the 16-coach Freight EMU has been developed specifically for transporting parcels and other goods at high speeds. The rake was developed by Chennai-based Integral Coach Factory. Also read: NFR installs weather stations to improve monsoon safety The freight train is equipped with several features aimed at improving the speed, safety and efficiency of logistics operations. These include advanced propulsion and braking systems, a roller floor system to facilitate parcel loading, automatic wide sliding doors and temperature-controlled facilities for goods requiring refrigeration. It also has CCTV surveillance and fire detection systems. Railway officials said the technical trials are aimed at carrying out a detailed assessment of the rake’s functionality, reliability and performance at high speeds. The 130 kmph trial is part of the testing process before the train can be considered for wider operational use. Successful completion of the trials could pave the way for faster and more reliable parcel and logistics transportation on the Indian Railways network. The introduction of a dedicated high-speed freight train based on the Vande Bharat platform is also aimed at improving the competitiveness of rail-based parcel transportation, particularly for time-sensitive goods. The latest trial marks another step in efforts to expand the use of semi-high-speed train technology beyond passenger services and into India's growing logistics sector.

articles.title: Hyderabad's Skyroot ties up with Redcliffe for space diagnostics - The Siasat Daily
articles.content: Hyderabad: Hyderabad-based Skyroot Aerospace has partnered with diagnostic services provider Redcliffe Labs to study how diagnostic materials behave in space, in what the companies describe as India’s first collaboration between the diagnostics and private space sectors. According to a report by the Times of India , the partnership will combine Redcliffe’s expertise in diagnostic research with Skyroot’s launch and orbital capabilities to evaluate the stability of dry diagnostic reagents in low Earth orbit. As part of the first mission, dubbed DRIFT-1, Redcliffe Labs will send samples of its dry reagents into orbit for 90 days, while an identical set will be retained on Earth for comparison. The findings are expected to help create a flight-heritage dataset that could inform the development of future diagnostic technologies for space missions as well as healthcare delivery in remote and challenging environments on Earth. The companies said the research could have applications in astronaut health monitoring, space-based diagnostics, microgravity life sciences studies and point-of-care testing for future human spaceflight missions. “A diagnostics leader taking its expertise to orbit is exactly the kind of use case we want to open up by opening space for all,” Skyroot co-founder and CEO Pawan Kumar Chandana said to the newspaper. He noted that the project could serve as an early step towards developing better healthcare solutions for astronauts in orbit. Dheeraj Jain, chairman and co-founder of Redcliffe Labs, said the partnership reflects India’s ability to combine scientific disciplines to address complex global challenges. “The most transformative breakthroughs often happen at the intersection of disciplines that rarely come together,” he said, adding that bringing together diagnostics and space technology could open up new avenues for research and innovation. articles.title: India's First Vande Bharat Freight Train Undergoes High-Speed Safety And Braking Trials
articles.content: Vande Bharat Express (Pic Via X) (Representative Image) India's first Vande Bharat freight train reached a peak speed of 145 kmph during trial runs on the Kota-Nagda-Sawai Madhopur railway section in Rajasthan. The 16-coach prototype, manufactured at Chennai's Integral Coach Factory, commenced comprehensive testing under the supervision of the Research Designs and Standards Organisation on the Delhi-Mumbai railway corridor. The freight Electric Multiple Unit has a maximum operational speed of 160 kmph and is undergoing progressive trials at speeds of 120, 130, 135 and 145 kmph. The train features a total payload capacity of 395 tonnes, with 14 wagons having 25-tonne capacity each and two driver-trailer wagons with 20-tonne capacity each. This represents a substantial advancement over conventional cargo trains, which typically operate at 60-70 kmph compared to the Vande Bharat freight train's average operating speed of 80-90 kmph. The rake includes two refrigerated vans for perishable goods, two non-driving trailer coaches and 12 parcel coaches, equipped with automatic plug doors, pneumatic retractable roller flooring and advanced braking systems. The train incorporates modern safety features including fire detection systems, CCTV surveillance and the Indian Railways' automated anti-collision system KAVACH. All doors automatically lock once the train crosses 5 kmph, and the train cannot move unless every door is fully secured. The high-speed freight service is expected to benefit sectors such as e-commerce, pharmaceuticals, agriculture and express logistics, where faster deliveries are critical for business operations.
